register.name: Tonga First Growth and Jobs Development Policy Financing
register.detail: World Bank IDA grant · Announced 30 September 2026 · First of a two-part programme
register.note: Budget support for reforms in skills, finance, business and the ocean.
register.text: Budget support from the International Development Association for reforms that expand digital payments and financial services, strengthen workforce skills and apprenticeships, improve conditions for private investment and enhance the management of Tonga’s ocean resources. It finances the budget as a whole rather than one standard; its reforms bear most on livelihood, through jobs and access to finance.

register.name: Sustainable Economic Corridors and Urban Resilience Project
register.detail: World Bank IDA grant · Announced 1 May 2026 · With ADB $80M and the Government of Tonga $25M, $145M in all
register.note: The World Bank share of a $145 million project for Greater Nukuʻalofa.
register.text: A grant from the International Development Association for a new climate-resilient bridge, upgraded roads that link the airport and the port, and drainage and water management systems that reduce flooding in key urban areas. Drier streets and safe evacuation routes protect homes, and better roads bring jobs, markets and essential services within reach: shelter and livelihood.

register.name: Second Fiscal, Disaster and Climate Resilience Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank IDA grant · Board approval announced 16 May 2025
register.note: Budget support for tax, energy efficiency, debt transparency and early warning.
register.text: Budget support from the International Development Association for reforms that reduce inefficient tax exemptions, introduce energy efficiency standards, improve debt transparency and enable disaster alerts by mobile phone, including in the remote outer islands. It finances the budget as a whole; its reforms bear on energy, through less reliance on imported diesel, and on the safety of every home when disaster strikes.

register.name: Safe and Resilient Schools, second additional financing
register.detail: World Bank IDA grant · Approved 5 December 2024 · Part of $21.25M with GPE and the Umbrella Facility
register.note: The IDA share of the second additional financing.
register.text: The second additional financing of the Tonga Safe and Resilient Schools Project, with the Global Partnership for Education and the Governments of Australia and New Zealand through the Papua New Guinea and Pacific Islands Umbrella Facility. It funds the construction, rehabilitation and maintenance of disaster-resilient classrooms, staff housing and water, sanitation and hygiene facilities, so education stays within reach after cyclones and tsunamis.

register.name: Health Enhancement and Resiliency in Tonga Project
register.note: Non-communicable diseases, primary care and a rebuilt hospital in Vavaʻu.
register.text: A grant for the Health Enhancement and Resiliency in Tonga (HEART) Project, which builds a system to prevent, detect and manage non-communicable diseases and strengthens primary health care with staff training, medical equipment and digital tools. It also rebuilds Prince Wellington Ngu Hospital in Vavaʻu with disaster-resistant, energy-efficient buildings, so health care holds up when disaster strikes.

register.name: First Fiscal, Disaster and Climate Resilience DPO with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 19 January 2024 · $5M development policy grant and a $20M Cat DDO
register.note: Budget support with funds that release when disaster strikes.
register.text: A US$25 million World Bank grant: a US$5 million development policy grant and a US$20 million catastrophe deferred drawdown option that Tonga can access immediately after a disaster. It finances the budget as a whole, and its rapid funds protect the spending on food, water, shelter and health that a cyclone or tsunami puts at risk.

register.name: Tonga Renewable Energy Project (FP090)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund grant, ADB the accredited entity · Approved 20 October 2018 · 100% disbursed
register.note: Battery storage for the grid and solar mini-grids for the outer islands.
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant for utility-scale battery storage that keeps the grid stable and green mini-grids in the outer islands, cofinanced by the Asian Development Bank, the Governments of Tonga and Australia and Tonga Power Limited. It serves energy: in 2025 the project connected all 84 households on Hunga Island and 37 households on ʻOʻua to solar power.

register.name: Pacific Regional Energy Security Emergency Assistance Project, Tonga grant
register.detail: ADB grant · Announced 12 October 2026 · Tonga’s share of $40.1M for three Pacific nations
register.note: Helps Tonga manage fuel price swings and keep electricity affordable.
register.text: Tonga’s grant under a $40.1 million Asian Development Bank emergency project for energy security in the Pacific, announced amid the Middle East crisis. It helps Tonga manage its exposure to fuel price volatility and maintain affordable electricity services through support to Tonga Power Limited, serving the energy standard.

register.name: Women Entrepreneurs Leveraging Innovative Finance in Tonga Project
register.detail: ADB grant, Asian Development Fund · Approved 16 December 2025
register.note: Credit and business opportunities for women.
register.text: An Asian Development Fund grant to expand credit access and unlock business opportunities for women. It supports the design of inclusive financial products, tailored support services and policies that advance private sector development, serving livelihood.

register.name: Sustainable Economic Corridors and Urban Resilience (SECURE) Project
register.detail: ADB grant · Approved 20 November 2025 · With the World Bank, $120M in grants
register.note: ADB-led; in ADB’s words, the largest development partner–financed project in Tonga’s history.
register.text: The ADB-led share of an integrated transport, urban and water infrastructure investment in Greater Nukuʻalofa, including a 720-metre lagoon bridge at Fangaʻuta, upgraded roads that link the airport and port, and urban drainage. It creates evacuation routes for disasters such as tsunamis and eases access to markets, serving shelter and livelihood.

register.name: Improving Economic Management Program (Subprogram 2)
register.detail: ADB policy-based grant, Asian Development Fund · Approved 23 October 2025 · Parallel cofinancing from Australia, New Zealand and the World Bank
register.note: Budget support for debt and revenue management and social protection.
register.text: A policy-based grant that strengthens debt and revenue management and reduces revenue leakages. It finances the budget as a whole and serves no single standard; it also expands coverage of the government’s social protection program.

register.name: Tonga Grid Enhancement for Sustainable Energy Transition Project
register.detail: ADB $1M, Clean Energy Fund $1.5M and EU $2.1M grants · Signed 20 November 2024 · Australia adds $5.6M in budget support
register.note: A 33 kV network to carry solar power, toward a 70% renewable target.
register.text: Grant agreements for a new 33 kilovolt network to evacuate energy from a solar power plant and an upgrade of part of the existing 11 kilovolt network, toward Tonga’s 70% renewable energy target. It reduces reliance on imported fossil fuels and makes the power grid more resilient to disasters, serving the energy standard.

register.name: Economic and Social Development Programme: solar power systems
register.detail: Japan grant aid · Notes signed and exchanged 10 December 2025 · Up to ¥400M
register.note: Solar power for the Tonga Broadcasting Commission’s early-warning network.
register.text: Grant aid from Japan for containerised solar power systems and pole-mounted transformers that strengthen the disaster early-warning and communication network of the Tonga Broadcasting Commission. It puts solar energy behind the warnings that protect every home when a cyclone or tsunami approaches.

register.name: Project for the Improvement of Fuaʻamotu International Airport
register.note: A larger terminal, a wider apron and a passenger boarding bridge.
register.text: A JICA grant to enlarge and upgrade the international terminal at Fuaʻamotu International Airport, repair damaged support columns, widen the international apron and add a passenger boarding bridge. It serves livelihood: the airport carries the visitors who earn almost half of Tonga’s export income.

items.text: Root crops, squash and vanilla on half the land.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 34.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.

items.name: MORDI Tonga Trust
items.text: A non-profit that supports women, youth and smallholder farmers in 122 rural communities, 80% of Tonga’s rural communities, with farm inputs and new technology for food and nutrition security.

items.name: Elemental Water Makers
items.text: A Dutch technology company whose solar-powered desalination systems, installed in 2026 on Hunga and Matamaka in Vavaʻu, can each produce up to 4,300 litres of drinking water a day, run by ten trained community members on each island with the Tonga Water Board.

items.name: Tonga Power Limited
items.text: Tonga’s electricity company, a co-financier of the Tonga Renewable Energy Project’s grid batteries and outer-island solar mini-grids; an ADB grant of October 2026 supports it in keeping electricity affordable.

items.name: SPBD Tonga
items.text: Lends to women micro-entrepreneurs with business training and asset-building support, and since 2025 offers its members home appliances at reduced prices through a partnership with Luna‘Eva & Sons Distributors.

items.name: Langafonua ʻa Fafine Tonga
items.text: The women’s organisation founded by Queen Sālote Tupou III launched a programme in 2025, Empowering Women in Handicraft Production, that trains women, girls and people with disabilities in traditional crafts such as tapa cloth and woven kiekie.

items.name: Digicel Pacific MyCash
items.text: Digicel’s mobile money service lets people in Tonga receive, store and spend money by mobile telephone, through an app or by USSD, and since 2025 allows customers without formal identification to register with basic information.
